children: Canada's main stock index rose on Tuesday, helped by gains for financial and telecommunication stocks, as oil pulled back from its highest level since April and investors looked ahead to a more seasonally favorable period for the market.
ended up 179.33 points, or 0.5%, at 36,107.96, stopping just short of Friday's closing level, which was the highest in over three weeks.

"You are entering one of the best seasonal periods of the year. November and December are historically pretty rewarding months, especially given the current environment that is really oversold from a breadth perspective," said Sid Mokhtari, chief market technician for CIBC Capital Markets.

settled 1.8% lower at $101.79 a barrel as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian president and Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure.
The move in oil helped lower interest rates, said Mokhtari, adding, "you bring rates lower then you start buoying the utilities and telcos — things that were hit hard with the recent rise in rates."
The Canadian 10-year yield (CA10YT=RR) eased 6.8 basis points to 3.894% after rising sharply on Monday as investors raised bets on a Bank of Canada interest rate hike next week.
The communication services index (.GSPTTTS) and heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) both rose 1%, while industrials ended 0.7% higher.
